- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above peak or adjust downward after 2–3 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; add 0.5–1.5% buffer below forecast to account for mean reversion.
- Model frequently underestimates long-term upward trends (especially >70) in the 30-day horizon; increase forecast by 1–3% for prices above 70.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model tends to lag behind true price movements; add 1–2 days of lag correction (i.e., forecast 1–2 days ahead of actual trend).
- If sentiment is high and price is near 70+, model often overcorrects downward; avoid sharp drops unless sentiment turns negative.
- For 30-day forecasts, if last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum, model often fails to capture it; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for each day of momentum.
